items.title: Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1958-09-02
items.q: Ed Bailey, because he had the band in World War I, in the 8th Regiment.

ctx.x: It was one grand theater. It was a grand theater, that was at 31st. I think it was the State Theater. It was a monogram. Yeah, it was a monogram, and it was the State Theater. The State, that's right. That's right.

What's going to have the band in there? Ed Bailey. Oh, I never knew. Yeah, well, he lives here now, he works at the post office. Ed Bailey, because he had the band in World War I, in the 8th Regiment. Well, I met Jimmy, he was crazy the way I played rhythm. He said if I show him how to do it, he learned me how to read. That's the first time I ever read a note. He gave me my first lessons of how to read, which I'm not a great reader now, but he gave me my idea of it. But all through New Orleans, I couldn't read a…
Jimmy Burtrain played xylophone too, didn't he? Oh, he's a good drummer.
